eventMetadata.context_description: Spain leads trader consensus at 15.6% implied probability for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, narrowly ahead of France (14.4%) and England (11.3%), reflecting the razor-thin margins in the latest FIFA rankings where France overtook Spain for No. 1 by just 0.92 points on April 1, with Argentina third at 1874.81. This bunched race persists due to deep talent pools, favorable group draws avoiding early elite clashes in the expanded 48-team format, and lingering injury concerns for stars like Rodrygo and Mbappé that introduce upset potential across a hyper-competitive knockout path.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom leads trader consensus at 27% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, bolstered by recent polls showing him ahead of Kamala Harris in California and tied for second in New Hampshire, highlighting his executive record as governor and prior national debate exposure against DeSantis. The field remains wide open, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 8.8% drawing progressive buzz amid DSA reelection support, and Jon Ossoff at 6.6% gaining from Georgia's battleground appeal. Over the past week, prospects like Harris—who signaled she's "thinking about" another run at Al Sharpton's National Action Network convention—and J.B. Pritzker courted Black voters in New York, signaling an early shadow primary. Consolidation could hinge on 2026 midterm outcomes for governors in swing states, fundraising dominance, and endorsements, as no clear frontrunner has emerged two years out.

title: The Masters 2026: Winner
description:
This polymarket will resolve according to the player who wins the 2026 Masters Tournament.

If this player is eliminated from contention for The Masters based on the official rules of the tournament, the relevant market will resolve to "No".

In the event of a tie, this market will resolve according to the official winner as determined by The Masters official tournament rules.

If no winner is announced by December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution sources will be the official results published by the PGA TOUR website and The Masters website. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Defending champion Rory McIlroy commands trader consensus at 70% implied probability to repeat at the Masters, holding a historic six-shot 36-hole lead at 12-under after a flawless second-round 65 featuring birdies on six of his last seven holes, building on his opening 67 that shared the lead with Sam Burns. This dominant Augusta National display, the largest 36-hole advantage since records began, echoes Tiger Woods' back-to-back wins in 2001-02 and reflects McIlroy's strong course history amid ideal weather with no delays. Chasers like Tommy Fleetwood (4.6%), Patrick Reed (4.0%), and Burns (3.3%) sit at 6-under via steady play—Reed's early par-5 eagles and Fleetwood's top-25 consistency—but face steep climbs on a firm, fast layout entering the weekend.

title: Fed decision in April?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's April 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for April 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their April meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders on Polymarket have priced a 98% implied probability of no Federal Reserve rate change at the April 29-30, 2026 FOMC meeting, reflecting robust consensus driven by March's hotter-than-expected CPI data—headline inflation at 3.3% year-over-year, up from 2.4%—and resilient labor market indicators, including 178,000 nonfarm payroll additions and a steady 4.3% unemployment rate. The March FOMC's decision to hold the federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75%, paired with a dot plot signaling just one cut for 2026 amid elevated inflation risks from oil shocks, has solidified this positioning. Upside surprises in upcoming April CPI or retail sales could further entrench the hold, though unexpectedly weak jobs data might marginally revive cut odds below 2%.

title: Military action against Iran ends on...?
description:
This market will resolve according to the next date Iran Standard Time (GMT+3:30), on which neither the US nor Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate. 

If the date/time of a qualifying strike cannot be confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting by the end of the third calendar day after the listed date, the respective market will resolve to "Yes" regardless of whether a strike is later confirmed to have occurred. If strikes could be verified under the prior rule for each listed day, this market will resolve to "Military action through April 30."

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be considered, regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US/Israeli ground operatives will not be considered.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

series.title: Military action against Iran ends on

eventMetadata.context_description: A US-Iran ceasefire agreement, brokered by Pakistan and effective April 8, has driven trader consensus to price "April 9" at 98% for the end of military action against Iran, as no confirmed US or Israeli airstrikes on Iranian soil have occurred since before the April 7 announcement. This follows over five weeks of joint US-Israeli operations under Operation Epic Fury, targeting Iranian military sites and nuclear facilities starting February 28, with the truce conditioned on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing peace talks. The ceasefire holds despite strains, including Trump warnings of renewed strikes if negotiations fail. Potential challenges include verified escalations, proxy attacks, or Hormuz disruptions extending action beyond the two-week window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance holds a slim edge in trader consensus for the 2028 presidential election at 18.8%, reflecting his position as President Trump's heir apparent, bolstered by topping the March 2026 CPAC straw poll and a recent UMass Lowell survey showing him leading California Gov. Gavin Newsom 33%-30% in a hypothetical matchup. Newsom trails closely at 17.1%, buoyed by his high-profile criticism of Trump administration policies and Democratic polling strength in California, amid post-2024 party reassessment. The race remains tightly contested this far out, with no primaries underway and fluid fields on both sides—Marco Rubio at 9.4% gains from his Secretary of State role. Midterm election outcomes in November 2026, formal announcements, and endorsements could widen gaps, while scandals or polling shifts introduce volatility in this open contest.

title: Next Prime Minister of Hungary
description:

eventMetadata.context_description: With Hungary's parliamentary election set for April 12, trader consensus on Polymarket heavily favors Péter Magyar at 70.5% implied probability to become next prime minister, driven by consistent polling leads for his center-right Tisza party over incumbent Viktor Orbán's Fidesz. Recent surveys, including Medián's latest showing Tisza at 58% versus Fidesz at 35% among decided voters, and the Politico Poll of Polls aggregate at 50%-39%, reflect a widening opposition edge amid undecided voter shifts. Magyar, a former Fidesz insider turned challenger, has unified anti-Orbán sentiment through intensive rural campaigning and countering smears, while Orbán faces backlash over corruption allegations and voter intimidation reports. Divergent polls persist, with some showing Fidesz ahead, underscoring election uncertainty until formal post-vote PM appointment.

eventMetadata.context_description: Miami Heat enter their road matchup against the Washington Wizards as strong trader consensus favorites, driven by Washington's brutal injury report listing eight players out—including D'Angelo Russell, Kyshawn George, and Cam Whitmore—severely thinning their rotation amid a tanking season. Heat dominated the April 4 head-to-head 152-136 at home, powered by Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s 32 points and blocks from Ware, despite recent defensive struggles and a loss to Toronto. Miami contends with Tyler Herro out (foot), Davion Mitchell questionable (shoulder), and Norman Powell doubtful (groin), but their 41-39 record keeps play-in hopes alive in the crowded East standings, while Wizards' home court and rest edge offer limited upset paths.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President J.D. Vance holds a slight edge as heir apparent in the early 2028 Republican presidential primary field following President Trump's second-term victory and constitutional term limits, but trader consensus on Polymarket prices Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as the narrow leader at 49% amid his high-profile HHS role advancing health policy reforms appealing to populist voters wary of establishment medicine. Secretary of State Marco Rubio trails at 21.1% after recent donor signals of preference over Vance and his hawkish stance contrasting Vance's restraint on the ongoing Iran conflict, as highlighted in a late-March CPAC straw poll where Vance led 53%-35%. The tight contest reflects Trump's kingmaker influence, with midterms, foreign policy outcomes, and potential endorsements poised to create separation among these administration insiders.

eventMetadata.context_description: With the Detroit Pistons having clinched the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference at 58-22, key factors driving trader consensus include potential load management and rest for stars like Cade Cunningham, who recently returned from a 10-game absence due to a collapsed lung and starred in their 137-111 rout of the Bucks on April 8. The Charlotte Hornets (43-37, ninth in East) host with home-court edge at Spectrum Center, aiming to gain momentum ahead of the play-in tournament, but face a Pistons squad winning four of five, including a 2-0 season series edge and 4-1 in recent head-to-heads. Minimal injury concerns on official reports, though back-to-back travel and playoff prep could influence rotations.
